subject: science
passage: The roving coral grouper, a reef fish of the Red Sea and the Indian ______ sometimes hunts with a partner of a different species. When prey hides in a crevice too narrow for the grouper to enter, the grouper may swim to a nearby moray eel and shake its head in a signal that researchers have described as an invitation; the eel then follows it to the hiding place and flushes the prey out. Biologists regard this as a rare example of cooperation across species in the wild.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "A reef fish of the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean" is extra information that renames the grouper. It opens with a comma after "grouper," so it must close with a comma too, before the verb "hunts." The semicolon later in the text joins two independent clauses and has no bearing on this boundary.
explanation.A: Correct. The closing comma matches the opening comma after "grouper" and completes the pair around the extra information.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Once the comma closes the extra information, "and sometimes hunts" is left with nothing to join to; the subject needs "hunts" as its own verb, not as a second item after "and."
explanation.C: Incorrect. Without a closing comma, the extra information is never set off and runs straight into the verb "hunts."
explanation.D: Incorrect. A semicolon can't separate the subject "The roving coral grouper" from its verb "hunts."
